chapter_summary: Proverbs 16 stands at the structural heart of the book and is dominated by one towering truth: God is sovereign over all human plans, steps, decisions, and outcomes. The chapter opens and closes with this theme — from the LORD directing the tongue (v. 1) to the LORD disposing of the lot (v. 33). In between, the chapter addresses pride (which God hates and punishes), the fear of the LORD (which turns people from evil), the surpassing value of wisdom over gold, the danger of trusting one's own judgment, and the crucial disciplines of controlling anger and governing one's spirit. Throughout, God is never a distant observer — He weighs hearts, directs steps, and rules over what looks like chance.
main_lesson: God is in charge of all our plans and steps. He hates pride and loves it when we trust Him with everything we do.

memory_verse.kjv: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
memory_verse.little_bible: You can make your plans. But it is God who guides every step you take.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 16 is one of the most theologically dense chapters in the entire book. It opens with a paradox: humans plan, but the LORD governs the outcome (v. 1, 9, 33). This is not fatalism — it is faith. God does not despise human planning; He directs it. The appropriate response is to commit our works to Him (v. 3) and to walk in the fear of the LORD (v. 6). These are not passive postures but active trust.

The chapter is particularly striking in its treatment of pride. Verse 5 calls pride in heart an 'abomination' — the same word used for idolatry. Verse 18 delivers the famous warning: 'Pride goeth before destruction.' Parents should help children understand that pride is not merely rudeness or boasting — it is a fundamental failure to acknowledge God's sovereignty and one's own dependence. Humility is not weakness; it is wisdom.

The kingship sayings (vv. 10–15) place enormous moral weight on leaders. Kings must be just, must hate wickedness, and must surround themselves with truth-tellers. These verses are an invitation to help children understand that leadership is a sacred trust, not a prize. Whether your child leads a sibling, a sports team, or a classroom one day, the standard is the same: righteousness, not power.

The chapter closes with a call to self-mastery: the person who rules their own spirit is greater than the mightiest warrior (v. 32). This is the wisdom that wins wars no army can fight — wars of anger, of fear, of pride. Help your children see that self-control is not a small thing. It is heroic. And in verse 33, God gets the final word: even what looks like random chance is in His hands.
application_for_children: This week, before you make any plan or decision, stop and say: 'God, You direct my steps. Help me choose what You want.' Practise handing your plans to God every morning.

verses.kjv: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD.
verses.little_bible: People plan in their hearts. But the words that come out are guided by God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God guides what we plan and what we say.
verses.meaning: Human planning and speech are not purely independent acts. Even our ability to think and articulate is ultimately under God's sovereignty. This opens the chapter's grand theme: God governs what seems most personal and internal to us.
verses.prayer: God, guide my thoughts and words today.
verses.discussion_question: Who is in charge of what we plan and say?
verses.family_discussion: How does it change how we speak and plan when we truly believe that God is involved even in our thoughts and words? What would it look like for our family to invite God into our daily planning?
verses.do_it_today: Before you speak about something important today, pause and ask God to guide your words. Try it at least once.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting quietly with hands folded, a gentle light from above resting on their heart and their lips, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but the LORD weigheth the spirits.
verses.little_bible: People always think their own choices look fine. But God sees the truth inside every heart.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: We think we are fine. God sees the real truth.
verses.meaning: Self-deception is one of the most dangerous spiritual conditions. People naturally judge themselves favourably, but God's assessment penetrates beyond behaviour to the spirit — the inner motive and character. This is a call to honest self-examination before God.
verses.prayer: God, show me the truth about my heart.
verses.discussion_question: Why can we not always trust what we think about ourselves?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate honest self-reflection in our children — the ability to ask 'Is my motive actually right here?' — without producing anxiety or shame?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing you did today. Ask yourself honestly: what was your real reason for doing it? Talk to God about what you find.
verses.illustration_prompt: God's hand holding a set of golden scales, gently weighing a glowing spirit, a child watching with humility, soft light, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
verses.little_bible: Give your work and your plans to God. He will make your thoughts steady and sure.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Give your plans to God. He will make them firm.
verses.meaning: Committing works to the LORD is an act of trust and surrender — handing over the outcome to God. The promise is that our thoughts (plans, purposes) will be established, made firm, and succeed under His direction. It is an invitation to collaboration with God.
verses.prayer: God, I give my plans and work to You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to give your plans to God?
verses.family_discussion: As a family, how do we practically commit our work — school, jobs, chores, projects — to the LORD? What would a family habit of daily surrender look like?
verses.do_it_today: Before you start your main task today, say out loud: 'God, I give this to You. Please guide it.' Then begin.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child lifting their hands upward with a small scroll of plans in their palms, a warm golden light receiving it from above, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: The LORD hath made all things for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
verses.little_bible: God made all things for His own purposes. Even those who do evil will face the day God has set.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God made all things for His purpose. Nothing is outside His plan.
verses.meaning: God's sovereignty is total — even the wicked, in their rebellion, are not outside His ultimate purposes. The 'day of evil' for the wicked is not an accident but a scheduled reckoning. This is a sobering but steadying truth: history is not random; God holds all of it.
verses.prayer: God, You are in control of everything.
verses.discussion_question: Is there anything that surprises God or is outside His plan?
verses.family_discussion: How does knowing that God is sovereign over even evil and injustice help us trust Him when we see bad things happening in the world?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing that worries or confuses you about the world. Remind yourself: 'God has a purpose. He is in control.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A vast starry sky with a gentle light holding the whole universe in an open hand, awe and wonder, soft watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD: though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
verses.little_bible: God hates a proud heart. Even if proud people join together, they will not escape His judgment.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hates pride. Proud people will be judged.
verses.meaning: Pride in heart — not mere confidence but the deep refusal to acknowledge God and one's dependence on Him — is called an abomination, the strongest term of divine disgust used in Proverbs. No alliance of the proud can shield them from God's judgment. Pride is ultimately a form of rebellion against God's sovereignty.
verses.prayer: God, keep pride far from my heart.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think God hates a proud heart so much?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children distinguish healthy confidence from the kind of pride God calls an abomination — the pride that pushes God out and lifts self up?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: is there anything I am proud of that I have not thanked God for? Thank Him for it right now.
verses.illustration_prompt: A puffed-up figure standing alone looking downward in shame, the light of God above turning away, humility contrasted nearby, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the LORD men depart from evil.
verses.little_bible: Mercy and truth clean away our sin and wrongdoing. Respecting God and His holiness turns people away from evil.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mercy, truth, and honouring God clean us from wrong.
verses.meaning: Sin is cleansed through a combination of divine mercy (God's loyal love) and truth (honest acknowledgment of wrongdoing). And the ongoing power to walk away from evil is the fear of the LORD — a deep reverence and holy awe that makes sin look foolish and costly. Both forgiveness and ongoing obedience are rooted in who God is.
verses.prayer: God, let fear of You keep me from evil.
verses.discussion_question: How does honouring God help us turn away from wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a genuine fear of the LORD in our family — not terror but holy awe that makes disobeying God feel deeply wrong and costly?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one wrong thing you keep being tempted to do. Ask God to make His holiness feel so real to you that you walk away from it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing at a fork in the road, one path dark and winding, one path lit and clear, choosing the lit path with God's light ahead, watercolour

verses.kjv: When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
verses.little_bible: When your life pleases God, He can even make your enemies calm and peaceful toward you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Please God, and He can even make enemies peaceful.
verses.meaning: God is not only able to bless the righteous; He can supernaturally reshape the attitudes of even hostile people toward those who walk in His ways. This is a remarkable promise: approval from God is the foundation for peace with people — even adversaries. Human approval-seeking is replaced by God-pleasing.
verses.prayer: God, help me please You in all I do.
verses.discussion_question: How does pleasing God affect our relationship with other people?
verses.family_discussion: When we are in conflict with someone, do we first ask 'Am I walking in ways that please God?' before trying to manage the relationship? How might that change things?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone who seems unfriendly toward you. Instead of trying to fix the relationship yourself, pray: 'God, let my life please You. You handle the rest.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children who looked like opponents now sitting peacefully together, a soft divine light between them, a sense of God-given peace, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.
verses.little_bible: A small amount earned honestly is better than a huge amount earned by doing wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A little earned honestly beats much gained wrongly.
verses.meaning: The measure of true value is not quantity but character. Wealth without righteousness is corrupted at its root. A small honest gain is genuinely better because it is unspoiled and carries God's blessing. This cuts against every worldly instinct to accumulate more at any cost.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose honesty over more money.
verses.discussion_question: Why is a little earned honestly worth more than a lot earned by doing wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a heart that genuinely values integrity over gain — especially when cheating or cutting corners seems to offer faster or greater results?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a time when someone got something by cheating. Did it really help them? Now think of honest work. Which feels better?
verses.illustration_prompt: A small simple meal on one side glowing with warmth, a grand feast on the other side surrounded by shadows and unease, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
verses.little_bible: You can make your own plans. But God is the One who guides every step you take.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: We plan our way. God guides our steps.
verses.meaning: Human planning is legitimate and good. But sovereignty over the outcome belongs to God alone. This is not a rebuke of planning but a call to hold our plans loosely, trusting that God's direction is wiser than our best ideas. It is one of the most quoted verses in all of Proverbs.
verses.prayer: God, guide every step I take today.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it good to plan but also trust God with the result?
verses.family_discussion: As a family, how do we model holding plans loosely before God — making wise decisions while remaining genuinely open to God redirecting our steps?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one plan you have. Under it write: 'God, this is Yours. Direct my steps.' Leave the outcome with Him.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking along a path with footprints glowing gently, a hand from above gently guiding the direction, wonder and trust, warm watercolour

verses.kjv: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.
verses.little_bible: A good king speaks with wisdom given by God. His judgments and decisions are right and true.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A good king speaks God's wisdom in all judgment.
verses.meaning: The ideal king speaks with a divine authority — his words in judgment carry the weight of God's wisdom. This is not a statement about every historical king but about the God-given standard: those who lead and judge must speak with truth, not partiality. Leadership speech carries sacred weight.
verses.prayer: God, give leaders around me true wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: What should a leader's words sound like when they are truly wise?
verses.family_discussion: How do we prepare our children to lead with words that are truthful, just, and wise — whether as a parent one day, a boss, or simply a friend others listen to?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a leader you look up to. What is it about their words that makes you trust them? Write it down.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise king on a simple throne speaking carefully to gathered people, golden light on his lips, a sense of truth and authority, watercolour style

verses.kjv: A just weight and balance are the LORD's: all the weights of the bag are his work.
verses.little_bible: God cares about fair scales and honest measures. Being fair in trade and business belongs to Him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fair weights and honest scales belong to God.
verses.meaning: In the ancient marketplace, weights were used to measure goods. Dishonest merchants used false weights. God claims ownership of just weights — meaning fairness in commerce is not just a social good but a theological one. Honesty in everyday transactions is worship.
verses.prayer: God, help me be fair and honest always.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God care about whether we are fair when we buy and sell things?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that honesty in money, business, and everyday exchanges is not just politeness but obedience to God who calls Himself the owner of fair scales?
verses.do_it_today: Check if you have been fully honest in any recent exchange — giving back correct change, keeping a promise about money. Fix anything that needs fixing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A pair of perfectly balanced golden scales glowing with warm light, a marketplace scene behind them, honest trade, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.
verses.little_bible: It is terrible when leaders do evil. Lasting rule and good authority can only be built on doing right.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good leaders do right. Wickedness destroys rule.
verses.meaning: Kings and rulers are not exempt from moral standards — they are bound by them more strictly. The throne — any position of authority — is only made secure and lasting when it is grounded in righteousness. Wickedness in leadership is not just sin; it is self-destruction.
verses.prayer: God, raise up leaders who love what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does a leader's character matter for how long they can lead well?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that power without righteousness is fragile — and that the most durable forms of leadership in history have been those grounded in truth and justice?
verses.do_it_today: Name one leader in history — good or bad. What did their character produce? Talk about it with a parent.
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong throne made of light and righteousness on one side, a crumbling dark throne on the other, contrast watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.
verses.little_bible: Good leaders love people who tell them the truth. Honest and right words delight those who lead well.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise leaders love honest, truthful words.
verses.meaning: Wisdom in leadership includes the wisdom to love truth-tellers. A king who delights in righteous lips creates a culture of honesty around him. Conversely, a leader who surrounds himself with flattery is heading toward ruin. This is a call both to truthful speech and to leadership that welcomes it.
verses.prayer: God, help me speak truth to those I serve.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important for leaders to love people who tell them the truth?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family culture where honest speech — even uncomfortable truth — is welcomed and not punished? What signals do we send when a child tells us something hard?
verses.do_it_today: Tell a parent or trusted adult one honest thing you have been holding back from saying. Speak it with kindness.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking honestly to a parent who leans in with a welcoming expression, light and warmth between them, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.
verses.little_bible: An angry king is very dangerous — like messengers bringing death! But a wise person knows how to calm that anger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A king's anger is dangerous. Wisdom calms it.
verses.meaning: Royal anger in the ancient world carried lethal consequences. The proverb is practical: wisdom does not ignore or inflame powerful anger — it seeks to calm it. This is not cowardice; it is skillful, life-preserving wisdom. The principle applies to any dangerous temper that must be navigated carefully.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom when people are angry.
verses.discussion_question: What is the wise way to respond when someone in authority is very angry?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to navigate conflict with authority wisely — knowing when to speak, when to be quiet, and how to de-escalate without compromising truth?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a time someone was very angry. What helped calm things down? What made it worse? Learn from what worked.
verses.illustration_prompt: A stormy royal hall with a king's face red with anger, a calm wise figure gently raising a hand in peace, the storm settling, watercolour

verses.kjv: In the light of the king's countenance is life; and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain.
verses.little_bible: When a good king smiles on you, there is life and blessing in it. His favour is like welcome rain after a dry season.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A good leader's favour is like life-giving rain.
verses.meaning: The favour of a good ruler is genuinely life-giving — it opens doors, provides protection, and brings blessing. The image of the 'latter rain' refers to the spring rains in Israel that were essential for a good harvest. Favour from the right person at the right time can change everything.
verses.prayer: God, let Your favour rest on me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it feel like when someone important smiles at you with approval?
verses.family_discussion: How do we ensure that our children feel the warmth of our favour and delight — not just correction — knowing that parental favour reflects something of God's own?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone you love today: 'I am so glad you are in my life.' Let them feel your favour.
verses.illustration_prompt: Gentle rain falling on a dry field, everything turning green and alive, a soft golden light from above, relief and joy, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!
verses.little_bible: Getting wisdom is far better than getting gold. Knowing and understanding is worth more than silver.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom is worth more than gold or silver.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' core assertions. Wisdom — the ability to live well before God — is more valuable than the greatest material wealth. Gold and silver are real goods, but they cannot guide a life, navigate sorrow, or stand before God. Wisdom does all of this and more.
verses.prayer: God, I want wisdom more than treasure.
verses.discussion_question: If you had to choose between wisdom and a bag of gold, which would you pick and why?
verses.family_discussion: How do we communicate to our children — in what we celebrate, what we prioritise, what we invest in — that wisdom matters more than money or success?
verses.do_it_today: List three things wisdom can give you that money cannot. Think hard about each one.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright glowing book of wisdom on one side, a pile of gold coins on the other, the wisdom clearly outshining the gold, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.
verses.little_bible: The path of a good person is to turn away from evil. Staying on that right path keeps your soul safe.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people turn from evil. It keeps them safe.
verses.meaning: The 'highway' of the upright is not a private path but a well-established road — a known, clear direction away from evil. Walking this path is not optional for the righteous; it defines them. And keeping to this way has a direct consequence: the preservation of the soul from harm.
verses.prayer: God, keep me on the right path always.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean for your soul to be kept safe by choosing what is right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see the choices they make every day as steps on a road — either moving toward God and life, or toward evil and harm?
verses.do_it_today: Draw a simple road. On one side write 'right choices' and on the other write 'wrong choices.' Mark where you want your steps to go.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright open highway stretching toward light, a child walking confidently on it, dark paths on either side turned away from, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
verses.little_bible: Pride leads straight to destruction. A puffed-up spirit falls hard every time.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride leads to destruction. Haughtiness brings a fall.
verses.meaning: One of the most quoted lines in all of Scripture. Pride — the refusal to acknowledge dependence on God and others — is not just morally wrong; it is practically self-destructive. It creates blindness to real dangers and resistance to correction, setting up a fall that the proud person never sees coming.
verses.prayer: God, save me from a proud spirit.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when being too proud led to something going very wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children identify pride in themselves — not just obvious boasting but the subtle refusal to admit mistakes, ask for help, or give God credit?
verses.do_it_today: Is there anything you have been proud about without giving God credit? Stop right now and thank God for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure standing tall on a high platform, the ground cracking beneath their feet, a gentle warning in the scene, humble watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.
verses.little_bible: It is better to be humble among simple and lowly people. That beats sharing riches with those who are proud.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Humble and lowly is better than proud and rich.
verses.meaning: The company of the humble — even if materially poor — is better than the gains of the proud. This is a direct counter-cultural statement: social climbing toward the proud and powerful is not wisdom. The humble places are often where God's blessing and genuine community are found.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose humble company.
verses.discussion_question: Why would being with humble people be better than sharing a prize with proud people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model for our children a genuine preference for humble, honest people over those with status or wealth — in our friendships, our admiration, and our choices?
verses.do_it_today: Look around you today. Is there someone humble and overlooked you could spend time with or encourage? Do it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting happily with simple, joyful humble friends in a small space, contrasted with a lonely proud figure surrounded by gold, watercolour

verses.kjv: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy is he.
verses.little_bible: The person who handles things wisely will find what is good. And the person who trusts in God will be truly happy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Handle things wisely. Trust God. Find true happiness.
verses.meaning: Two habits are paired here: wise handling of situations and active trust in the LORD. Together they produce good outcomes and happiness — not as a formula but as the natural fruit of a life oriented toward wisdom and God. Happiness is not luck; it is the result of wise, trusting living.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You for true happiness.
verses.discussion_question: What is the connection between trusting God and being truly happy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children look for genuine happiness in God and wisdom rather than in temporary things that feel good but do not last?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing that made you genuinely happy this week. Thank God for it — and see if it came from wise or trusting choices.
verses.illustration_prompt: A cheerful child making a thoughtful decision and then smiling with genuine joy, soft light from above, warm and peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wise in heart shall be called prudent: and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.
verses.little_bible: The wise person is known for good thinking and careful choices. Sweet and pleasant speech helps others learn more.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise hearts and sweet words help people learn.
verses.meaning: Wisdom in the heart produces a reputation for prudence — thoughtful, careful, practical wisdom. And the manner of speech matters too: sweet, clear, pleasant words increase a person's effectiveness as a teacher and influence. Wisdom is both inner (heart) and outer (lips).
verses.prayer: God, make my heart wise and my words sweet.
verses.discussion_question: How do kind and clear words help people learn better?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model for our children that the way we communicate — gently, clearly, warmly — is as important as the content of what we are trying to teach?
verses.do_it_today: Teach someone something today — but make sure your words are kind and clear, not impatient. See how much better they receive it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise teacher speaking warmly to a small group of children, glowing words flowing from their lips like honey, warm learning scene, watercolour

verses.kjv: Understanding is a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools is folly.
verses.little_bible: Understanding is like a well of fresh water — it keeps giving life. But when foolish people try to teach, they just spread foolishness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Understanding is a life-giving well. Fools only teach folly.
verses.meaning: Understanding — deep, God-rooted comprehension — is a perpetually renewing source of life for those who possess it. It does not run dry. But a fool's attempt to instruct only multiplies folly; they cannot give what they do not have. This is a sobering warning about who we allow to shape us.
verses.prayer: God, give me understanding that never runs dry.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to learn from wise people and not from foolish ones?
verses.family_discussion: Who are the voices shaping our children's thinking — through media, friends, school? Are those voices sources of wisdom and life, or sources of folly?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one person in your life who is truly wise. Make time to learn from them this week.
verses.illustration_prompt: A deep glowing well with clear water rising up, a child drinking from it with joy, wisdom and life radiating from the water, watercolour style

verses.kjv: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.
verses.little_bible: A wise person's heart trains their mouth what to say. Their words keep adding to what others can learn.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A wise heart trains the mouth to speak well.
verses.meaning: The connection between heart and speech is direct: wisdom flows from an inward formation and expresses itself through the mouth. The wise person does not just have information to share — their very lips become an ongoing source of growth for those around them. Character shapes communication.
verses.prayer: God, form my heart to shape my words.
verses.discussion_question: How does what is in your heart come out through what you say?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that guarding what goes into their heart — what they read, watch, listen to — directly shapes what comes out of their mouth?
verses.do_it_today: Pay attention to your words today. Notice when something good or something bad comes out — and trace it back to what is in your heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A glowing heart connected by a gentle stream to a child's open lips, light and wisdom flowing from heart to words, soft watercolour

verses.kjv: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
verses.little_bible: Kind and gentle words are like honey. They are sweet inside and they actually make you healthier.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Kind words are sweet and heal like honey.
verses.meaning: The image of the honeycomb — rich, natural, sweet, and nourishing — captures what kind words do. They do not merely feel nice; they have real restorative power for the soul and body. The connection between word-environment and health is recognized here as both spiritual and physical.
verses.prayer: God, fill my mouth with pleasant words.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when someone's kind words made you feel better?
verses.family_discussion: How intentional are we about the quality of words in our home? Are our daily words sweet and life-giving, or are they often harsh, careless, or cutting?
verses.do_it_today: Say something genuinely kind and encouraging to every person in your home today. Watch what happens.
verses.illustration_prompt: A golden honeycomb dripping with honey, warm light around it, a child smiling as sweet words float around them, health and joy, watercolour

verses.kjv: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
verses.little_bible: A path can look completely right to a person. But that same path can lead straight to death in the end.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some paths look right but lead to death.
verses.meaning: This is a warning of the gravest kind: human moral intuition can be profoundly deceived. A path that feels right, looks right, and seems logical can end in ruin. This is not an argument against reason but a call to test all paths against God's Word, not merely personal feeling.
verses.prayer: God, show me when I am wrong about my path.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it dangerous to trust only your own feelings about what is right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop the habit of testing their instincts and feelings against God's Word — rather than assuming that whatever feels right to them must be right?
verses.do_it_today: Is there a decision you are making right now that feels right to you? Ask a wise parent or leader: 'Does this look right to you too?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright inviting path that curves and darkens sharply at the end, a warning sign in the distance, a child looking uncertain, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: He that laboureth laboureth for himself; for his mouth craveth it of him.
verses.little_bible: A working person works for their own good. Their hunger drives them to keep going and not give up.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hunger drives a person to work hard.
verses.meaning: This is an observation about motivation: physical need is itself a driver of productive work. The desire for food compels the worker not to be idle. There is no shame in working for one's own needs — God built hunger into humans as a prompt to diligent labour.
verses.prayer: God, give me a heart that works hard.
verses.discussion_question: What motivates you to do the work that needs to be done?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop intrinsic motivation to work — not just for reward but because diligence is part of how God made us and what glorifies Him?
verses.do_it_today: Do one chore or piece of work today without being asked. See how it feels to work with a willing heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child working with diligence in a garden or kitchen, a sense of purposeful effort and satisfaction, warm afternoon light, watercolour style

verses.kjv: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips there is as a burning fire.
verses.little_bible: A wicked person works to stir up trouble and evil. Their words burn like fire and destroy everything they touch.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wicked people dig up trouble. Their words burn like fire.
verses.meaning: The ungodly person does not merely stumble into wrongdoing — they dig for it, actively seeking evil to bring up and spread. Their speech is the weapon: burning, destructive, consuming. This is a portrait of someone whose whole energy is directed toward harm.
verses.prayer: God, keep my words from burning others.
verses.discussion_question: How can words burn and destroy like a fire?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that gossip, slander, and stirring up trouble with words is genuinely wicked — not just socially awkward — and carries real consequences?
verses.do_it_today: Check your words from today. Did any of them dig up trouble or burn someone? If so, go and make it right.
verses.illustration_prompt: A burning torch in the hands of a shadowed figure, words flying from their mouth like sparks setting things alight, danger and darkness, watercolour

verses.kjv: A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.
verses.little_bible: A troublemaker plants seeds of fighting wherever they go. A gossip can break apart the closest friendships.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Troublemakers cause strife. Gossip breaks friendships.
verses.meaning: Two related figures: the contentious person who seeds conflict openly, and the whisperer who does it covertly. Both destroy relationships. The whisperer is particularly dangerous because their damage is subtle — close friends separated by quiet words spoken behind backs.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from gossip and strife.
verses.discussion_question: How can whispering or gossiping break apart good friendships?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children the seriousness of gossip — not as a minor social failing but as a sin that can permanently destroy relationships that took years to build?
verses.do_it_today: If you have shared something about someone that you should not have, go and fix it. Do not let a whisper separate you from a friend.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two friends being pulled apart by shadowy whispering words between them, sadness on their faces, the damage gossip does, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way that is not good.
verses.little_bible: A violent and dangerous person draws others in. They lead those nearby into paths that are harmful and wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Bad people lead others into dangerous wrong paths.
verses.meaning: Violence and wickedness are not contained to the violent person — they have a recruiting quality. The dangerous person entices and pulls others along a harmful path. Peer influence toward evil is real and serious. This is a warning both to resist such influence and to guard who we allow near us.
verses.prayer: God, protect me from dangerous friendships.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever been pulled toward something wrong by a friend? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop the courage and discernment to recognise when someone is leading them the wrong way — and to walk away even if it feels costly?
verses.do_it_today: Think about who you spend the most time with. Do they lead you toward good or toward trouble? Talk to a parent if you are not sure.
verses.illustration_prompt: A shadowy figure pulling a child down a dark path, a gentle warning light in the background showing the right way, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He shutteth his eyes to devise froward things: moving his lips he bringeth evil to pass.
verses.little_bible: The troublemaker closes their eyes to scheme and plan evil. Then with their moving lips they carry out the wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Schemers plan evil and then carry it out.
verses.meaning: This verse describes the deliberate, premeditated nature of certain evil: eyes closed to think, lips moving to execute. This is not accidental wrongdoing — it is calculated wickedness. The picture makes it clear that sin here is intentional, not a stumble but a scheme.
verses.prayer: God, keep my mind from scheming evil.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between making a mistake and planning to do something wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that planned wrongdoing carries a different moral weight — and that the moment we start scheming how to do something wrong, we need to stop and turn to God?
verses.do_it_today: If you have been thinking about doing something you know is wrong, stop. Talk to God about it right now before it goes further.
verses.illustration_prompt: A hunched figure with closed eyes scheming, dark thoughts visible above their head, a sense of foreboding and warning, watercolour style

verses.kjv: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.
verses.little_bible: White hair and old age are a crown of glory — but only when that life has been lived in God's right ways.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Old age is glorious when lived in righteousness.
verses.meaning: Grey hair is honourable — but the honour is conditional. Old age that has been spent in righteousness is a glorious crown; old age spent in wickedness is not honoured by this proverb. A long life rightly lived is one of the most beautiful things imaginable. This is also a call to the young: build now for a glorious later.
verses.prayer: God, let me live righteously all my days.
verses.discussion_question: What would it look like to live in a way that makes old age something glorious?
verses.family_discussion: Who in your extended family or community has aged gloriously in righteousness? What can we learn from their life? Make time to honour them.
verses.do_it_today: Visit, call, or write to an older person you respect. Ask them: 'What is the most important thing you have learned about living right?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A beautiful elderly person with white hair glowing with dignity, a crown of gentle light on their head, warmth and peace surrounding them, watercolour

verses.kjv: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
verses.little_bible: Being slow to anger is better than being the strongest warrior. Ruling your own spirit is greater than conquering a whole city.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Controlling your anger is greater than winning any battle.
verses.meaning: This verse makes a stunning claim: self-mastery is greater than military mastery. The ancient world celebrated the warrior who conquered cities. Proverbs declares that ruling one's own spirit — controlling anger, appetite, impulse — is the greater achievement. Inner victory is harder and more honourable than outer conquest.
verses.prayer: God, help me rule my own spirit well.
verses.discussion_question: Why is controlling your own anger harder than winning a fight?
verses.family_discussion: How do we celebrate self-control in our home — slow anger, patient responses, governed emotions — with the same energy we celebrate outward achievements?
verses.do_it_today: The next time you feel anger rising today, stop before responding. Take three slow breaths. Practice ruling your spirit.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing tall and calm with fists unclenched while a storm of emotion swirls around them, inner peace and strength, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD.
verses.little_bible: People might throw dice or cast lots to decide something. But it is always God who decides what the answer truly is.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Even chance belongs to God. He decides all things.
verses.meaning: The lot — an ancient way of making decisions, like rolling dice — appears random. But the proverb declares that God governs even the lot. Nothing is truly random; nothing is outside His sovereign direction. This closes the chapter as it began: with total, reassuring divine sovereignty over every detail of human life.
verses.prayer: God, nothing is outside Your hand.
verses.discussion_question: Is there anything that happens by accident that God does not see or control?
verses.family_discussion: How does it change our anxiety about uncertain things — decisions, test results, the future — to know that God governs even what looks random or accidental?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing in your life that feels uncertain or out of control right now. Write it down and write beside it: 'God holds this.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A hand casting a lot or stone into the air, a gentle divine hand above it all holding the outcome, peace and trust, simple warm watercolour
